claims.claim: Reviewers describe a steep learning curve with complex mechanics, AI enemies, and game knowledge required to improve.

citations.review_text:
Amazing game with a very unique gameplay loop.

The gunfights in this game are unlike anything else. The slower rate of fire makes every shot count, forcing you to think twice before pulling the trigger. Positioning, sound awareness and knowing when to engage or disengage it's important.

The mechanics are pretty unforgiving, but that's exactly what makes the game fun. Be warned, though: it has a very steep learning curve, with a lot of mechanics, enemies and game knowledge to learn before you can really get comfortable.

Even the AI enemies require some knowledge to deal with efficiently, as different enemies have different weaknesses and ways of being dealt with. And while you're busy taking care of them, you always have to keep an eye out for other players who might be listening to every sound you make.

Despite all the good things this game has to offer, there are three main issues I have with it.

1. Content

Things have improved now that the studio has decided to focus its resources on this game, but even so, there are still periods where absolutely nothing is going on. No events, no seasons, no new content, nothing. Sometimes it feels like the game just enters a content drought and stays there for a while.

2. Bush campers

This is probably one of my biggest frustrations. The game increasingly feels like a horror game where you never know when a bush is going to jumpscare you with a headshot from 6 km away.

And while this has improved somewhat, the main difference nowadays is that instead of getting shot from 6 km away by a silenced sniper rifle, you get shot from 6 km away by an unsilenced sniper rifle.

3. Cheaters

Unfortunately, the game has recently been dealing with waves of cheaters who repeatedly show up in matches using aimbot and wallhacks. It's particularly frustrating since it stopped being once in a while to a couple times a day.

Thankfully, they're usually fairly easy to report, and the developers are actively working on the issue. Hopefully, …

This can be a cruel game.. But it is also unbelievably rewarding to come out of a firefight and get some loot before escaping the map with your life (meaning you get to keep your character).  Once you learn more or less how to deal with npc mobs and the emviroment.. you'll just get better. This game comes with a huge learning curve to most. But it is an amazing game!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that solo play is punishing, tedious, and difficult compared to playing in teams.

citations.review_text:
A Unique Masterpiece Undermined by Its Own Systems

Hunt: Showdown 1896 remains one of the most uniquely tense tactical shooters on PC, presenting an atmosphere and audio framework that no other game can match. However, your enjoyment of this brutal extraction shooter depends almost entirely on who you play with, as a frustrating matchmaking system and a severe lack of permanent game modes drag down an otherwise brilliant experience.
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+

| The Good                           | The Bad                            |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+

| • Masterful PC gunplay & audio    | • Wildly inconsistent matchmaking  |
| • Highly rewarding team play       | • Punishing, tedious solo experience|
| • Mechanically unique atmosphere   | • Barely any permanent game modes  |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+

The Friend Factor: Duo/Trio Brilliance vs. Solo Misery

On PC, where precision aiming elevates the stakes, Hunt is a masterpiece when played with a dedicated group of friends. Coordinating flanks, managing sound discipline, and executing dynamic pushes in duos or trios showcases the game at its absolute best.
Playing solo, however, feels like a completely different—and often miserable—game. While Crytek gives solo players certain trait advantages, going alone turns Hunt into an exhausting, hyper-passive waiting game. One wrong step means immediate death with zero room for error, pushing solo play into a tedious, ultra-stealth playstyle that strips away the dynamic fun of team firefights.

Horrible Matchmaking

The biggest barrier to enjoying the game consistently is its wildly erratic matchmaking system.
• On the Steam Community Forums, players frequently complain that the Matchmaking Rating (MMR) is fundamentally broken, regularly throwing lower-tier players or casual duos into lobbies wi…
угарненько в пати, и иногда страшненько, в соло утомительно

After around 12 hours in Hunt: Showdown 1896, I can say it is a really well-made extraction shooter. It has much more going on than simply loading into a match, killing a few people, and extracting. The atmosphere, the tension, and the way every match can play out differently make it stand out from other games in the genre.

Playing with random teammates can be fun, but it is not always reliable. Sometimes you get good communication and exciting matches; other times, it can be frustrating. Solo play is honestly not for me. It feels scary and often boring, especially because you are usually fighting against duos or trios alone. You need a lot of patience and confidence to enjoy that mode.

I would mainly recommend Hunt: Showdown 1896 to friends who can play together and to experienced shooter players. With a team, the game becomes much more fun and memorable. It is challenging, tense, and rewarding when things go well.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the matchmaking as placing newer or lower-ranked players against highly experienced or high-level opponents.

citations.review_text:
Hunt: Showdown 1896: A Frustrating Experience for New Players

My experience with *Hunt: Showdown 1896* has been quite disappointing. While the game features an excellent setting and interesting mechanics, the multiplayer experience can be extremely frustrating—especially when you are still learning the ropes.

One of the biggest issues I encountered concerns matchmaking in three-player teams. You may end up paired with two experienced players who expect you to perform at their level, failing to consider that you are still a beginner. When things go wrong, instead of offering help, they might hurl insults, blame you for the defeat, or even actively troll you.

Worst of all is encountering teammates who deliberately refuse to revive you, abandon you mid-match, or simply run off, leaving you behind. What is the point of a cooperative game if your own teammates can turn the experience into a humiliating ordeal?

Compounding this is the frustration of facing "Prestige 100" players—opponents with a massive experience advantage—alongside the persistent concern regarding cheaters, an issue Crytek has officially acknowledged through their own ban reports.

The problem isn't losing; defeat is a natural part of any competitive game. The issue is that, all too often, you don’t feel like you’re learning or competing on fair terms—instead, you feel punished for being a beginner, sometimes even by the very people who are supposed to be your teammates.

*Hunt: Showdown 1896* has potential, but its community can be deeply toxic, and the experience for newcomers leaves much to be desired. A lack of camaraderie, intentional abandonment, verbal abuse, and vast gaps in experience levels can make playing with strangers far more unpleasant than it is enjoyable.

I do not recommend this game to those seeking a friendly cooperative experience or hoping to learn at their own pace. While the game’s core concept may be excellent, the actual experience of playing with random teammates can be …

Hunt: Showdown 1896 is easily the most recommended game in my Steam library.

Nothing else comes close to delivering the same hardcore competitive experience, with its unique Wild West and post-apocalyptic atmosphere combined with an extraction shooter gameplay loop.

[h1]Hunt: Showdown 1896 – 10/10. We Had a Plan. Then Honza Shot a Lantern.[/h1]
I started playing Hunt: Showdown back in its early days with two friends, Honza and Jirka.

We were supposed to be professional bounty hunters.
Unfortunately, our team had certain organisational difficulties.

I was the one making plans, marking enemy positions, coordinating movements, and trying to keep everyone alive.

Jirka was our professional loot goblin. If there was something worth stealing, he'd find it. If a firefight started, he'd usually find an excellent reason to be somewhere else.

And Honza?
Honza was a walking declaration of war.

One day, during what was supposed to be a carefully coordinated operation, he accidentally shot a lantern. The lantern ignited some oil. The oil ignited nearby barrels. The barrels exploded.
Our stealth operation was now a public announcement to the entire goddamn server.

[b]Fuck it. Fix bayonets. We're going in.[/b]

And that's how many of our hunting expeditions went.

[h2]When the Bayou Was Truly Terrifying[/h2]
What made the original Hunt special to me was its atmosphere.

The dark, oppressive Louisiana swamps, abandoned buildings, disturbing creatures, incredible sound design, and fascinating lore created something genuinely unique.

It wasn't simply another multiplayer shooter with monsters.

It was a brutal, atmospheric experience where every gunshot mattered, every mistake could get you killed, and sometimes the smartest decision was to stay quiet and listen.
I loved that feeling.

The maps seemed dangerous and alive. Even moving between objectives demanded attention.

And when another team appeared, things could turn ugly very quickly.

[h2]Old Guns, Bad Decisions, and Beautiful Chaos[/h2]
I loved the weapons.

Sniper rifles, powerful single-shot firearms, the Henry-style rifle, revolvers, bayonets, dynamite, and explosives.

There was something incredibly satisfying about the slower pace of historical gunfights. You couldn't simply sp…

Steep learning curve that may scare you away at first (we have all been there) but easily the best PvPvE extraction shooter out there. 

The gunplay feels very satisfying, the sound design is immaculate, and overcoming that initial learningc curve is super rewarding. Over time you realise that aim is not what will always win you fights and that's the best feeling ever imo (take this from a person with terrible aim that often clutches or manages to still rez teamates in a 1v2/1v3)

Some aspects can be improved further around the bounty and economy, such as the value of the bounty itself or the fact that some of the currencies feel a bit pointless with the re-balancing of events, but overall is not something that'd ruin you gameplay experience at all.

If you are looking for a game that has lots of action and honestly fun combat, this is definitely one of them. I have had this game for a few years now and always find myself returning off and on throughout the years.

100's of hours ago I thought I would only write a review if I hit a 1000's hours, as that's a good amount of playtime for a game like this.
Hunt is IMO the best type of game like this around, it's very light on extraction elements but with genre defining gunplay.

In Hunt the best aim does not always win, when to pick a fight is the most important aspect of this game, so the learning curve is immense and you will never truly master it, with every loss something new is learned, a peak, a gap in a wall, an audio cue, positioning, when to retreat or push, it's a methodical dance between Hunters. You can be an aggressive player or passive, and that's why it's fantastic as it caters for all game styles.

Just be prepared to die allot early on, but as you play your own style will come through and you will start getting kills.

You can play solo or in a team of 2 or 3, and this doesn't mean as a solo you play only against other solo's, no, you will fight against teams of 2 or 3 and get slaughtered, but persist and you will become a lethal hunter, and it all goes back to knowing when to pick a fight, wiping teams as a solo there is nothing else like it in gaming. Just make sure to play in teams, as for me it feels like a different playstyle from solo, and in teams you will get into more gunfights which helps with gun knowledge.

I could talk about this game all day, the Audio is amazing, you learn to track Hunter's through sound alone, very much like the old days of Doom and Quake where hearing a player pick up a first aid kit revealed their location and you knew they would run this way into your crosshairs. In Hunt a Hunter will jump over a fence and it leaves a mark, these subtle audio/visual clues which you pick up will push you towards becoming a better Hunter, and the better you become the more immersed you feel into Hunt's world and lore.

"Hunt giveth, Hunt taketh away"

Best game ever.

I've never reviewed a Steam game, but after over 3000 hours of enjoyment with Hunt: Showdown, I feel like I'm obligated. I'll explain why this is downright my favorite shooter. Hunt:Showdown is an extraction shooter based in the late 1800s in the Louisiana bayou (with a Colorado map as well) that includes dark fantasy elements that make up both the 'E' in "PVPVE" and some abilities granted to your player that really complement the gunplay mechanics.

The Gunplay
The arsenal primarily consists of weapons available in that time period, with a few that are somewhat of a creative twist (like the bomb lance, a harpoon that can be used as a melee weapon or shot as a projectile). These weapons consisting of bolt and lever action rifles, non-automatic shotguns (mostly), revolvers, crossbow, bow and arrow, and a plethora of melee weapons, create a vastly different dynamic than your typical shooter with multiple fully automatic options. It encourages more of a flick-style of gunplay that rewards clean shots over spamming. Coming from more modern shooters, I really did have to get accustomed to this and found great satisfaction in finally getting the hang of them. 

The Maps/Compounds
From an aesthetic point of view, they've done a fantastic job. From old mines, churches, farms, and more, they leave little to be desired. These compounds slot well into the swampy or mountainy maps in which they're placed. From a tactical/balance standpoint, I can only name one or two compounds…

Over time you realise that aim is not what will always win you fights and that's the best feeling ever imo (take this from a person with terrible aim that often clutches or manages to still rez teamates in a 1v2/1v3)

Some aspects can be improved further around the bounty and economy, such as the value of the bounty itself or the fact that some of the currencies feel a bit pointless with the re-balancing of events, but overall is not something that'd ruin you gameplay experience at all.

claims.claim: Reviewers complain that recent ping restrictions and matchmaking changes create long queue times and poor connection experiences for players in regions without local servers.

citations.review_text:
The time has come to say goodbye. It's been fun while it lasted.

Unfortunately, it seems the developers have completely forgotten about the players who don't have access to local servers. Ever since the implementation of the new ping restrictions, matchmaking has become an absolute joke.

Players in regions without local servers are now forced to sit through ridiculously long queue times just to find a game. All because of a ping system that seems to punish players for something completely beyond their control.

It's incredibly disappointing to see a game we genuinely love being ruined by decisions that completely disregard a portion of its player base.

We supported this game, invested countless hours into it, and stuck around through its ups and downs. But apparently, players like us don't matter.

A massive thank you to the developers for taking a game we loved and making it increasingly impossible for us to enjoy.

It's been a good run, but enough is enough.

Goodbye, Hunt: Showdown.

+The games sound, grafics, skins very good. 
+Takes time to get a hold how weapons, distance, sounds work.
-Playerbase full of cheaters and the developers don't do anything about it. (Streamers shown facts and the "team" didn't react.)
-Bug don't get fixet until next battlepass time limit.
-Sudden crash come and go (No resson why&what fix it after several days)
-Regional cross don't work. Servers full or "cube" names ect.

Sum: Play as a team of 3 its fun, weekdays and between 11:00-17:00 (after that its a nightmare in EU).  How much i loved the game, the dissapointed i got. If anyone feels like trying out, watch few streamers for a week and if still feels like go, take that ride. Invest few rounds only a day.
